comments.author: telotortium
comments.story_title: Unlearning descriptive statistics
comments.why_zh: 解释了为什么用户经常会在多个依赖上碰到罕见的坏情况延迟
comments.quote_zh: Gil Tene 有一个完整的演讲专门讲这一点，叫 “How NOT to measure latency”
comments.text_zh: Gil Tene 有一个完整的演讲专门讲这一点，叫 “How NOT to measure latency”（[VIDEO]）。在很多情况下，一个 web 服务（无论是服务端还是客户端）都有大量依赖，所以用户只要在某个依赖上碰到第 95 百分位延迟，整体延迟就会受到显著影响。换句话说，用户可能在大多数请求中都遇到“罕见”的坏情况。因此，为了真正把 web 服务的整体延迟控制住，甚至连更高的百分位也应该被严格控制。
comments.text: Gil Tene has an entire talk about this point called "How NOT to measure latency" ( [VIDEO] ). In many circumstances, a web service (either server or client) has large numbers of dependencies, so a user only has to hit 95th-percentile latency for one dependency to have their overall latency significantly hurt. In other words, users may encounter the "rare" bad case on a majority of requests. Thus, even higher percentiles should be tightly controlled in order to truly keep a web service's overall latency under control.

comments.author: sitkack
comments.story_title: Sanic – Python 3.5+ web server that's written to go fast
comments.why_zh: 关于平均值为何在延迟上会误导的延伸阅读
comments.text_zh: 处理时间时，你几乎从来都不该把平均值当作指标。对于时间，95 或 99 百分位延迟衡量的是每一百个请求中有多少个低于你的指标。尤其是当你测量的东西是更大系统的一部分时，这才是关键，因为一个资源会反过来请求 k 个更多资源。每个请求都有同等机会超过该延迟百分位。即使只有 10 个请求，也只有 90% 的会话会低于 99% 延迟。另见，Gil Tene [VIDEO] 一篇不错的概述，[LINK] 另见，[LINK]
comments.text: You almost never want to use average as your metric when dealing with time. For time, the 95 or 99 percentile latency is going to be measure of how many requests out of a hundred a less than your metric. Esp when the thing you are measuring is a piece of larger system, which is the crux, because of how a resource in turn requests k-more resources. Each request has an equal chance of being over the latency percentile. Even at 10 requests, only 90% of sessions will be under the 99% latency. See also, Gil Tene [VIDEO] A nice overview, [LINK] See also, [LINK]

comments.author: atombender
comments.story_title: K6: Like unit testing, for performance
comments.why_zh: 被引用来支持“监控工具会错误测量延迟尖峰”这一论点
comments.quote_zh: Gil Tene（Azul Systems）令人信服地论证过
comments.text_zh: K6 能处理 coordinated omission 问题吗？Gil Tene（Azul Systems）令人信服地论证过 [1]（幻灯片 [2]）：监控工具在延迟测量上出了问题，因为突然的尖峰由于取平均和百分位数的错误使用，没有被正确地体现在计时里。他认为百分位数根本没有用，因为从统计上看，大多数请求会经历大于等于 99.99 百分位的响应时间。所有百分位数都在撒谎；唯一真正有用且现实的数字其实是第 100 百分位。他还认为，展示延迟最能说明问题的方式是完整的直方图。我还没用过 K6，但一直在找好的负载测试工具，打算试一试。[1] [VIDEO] [2] [LINK]
comments.text: Does K6 deal with the coordinated omission problem? Gil Tene (Azul Systems) has argued convincingly [1] (slides [2]) that monitoring tools get latency measurement wrong because sudden spikes aren't represented correctly in timings because of averaging and the wrong use of percentiles. He argues that percentiles simply aren't useful, because, statistically, most requests will experience >= 99.99-percentile response times. All percentiles lie; the only truly useful and realistic number is, in fact, the 100th percentile. He also argues that the most revealing way to show latency is with a complete histogram. I haven't used K6 yet, but I've been looking for a good load-testing tool, and intend to try it out. [1] [VIDEO] [2] [LINK]
